chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from a number of our companions, who said:

When Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام passed away, Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام ordered that a lamp be kept in the house in which he had lived, until Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام passed away. Then Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام ordered the like of that in the house of Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, until he was taken with it to al-ʿIrāq. Then I do not know what happened.

key_terms.أُخْرِجَ: was taken out; referring to being taken to al-ʿIrāq
key_terms.السِّرَاجِ: the lamp that was ordered to be kept in the house
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the residence in which the Imam had lived
key_terms.الْعِرَاقِ: Iraq, the destination mentioned in the narration
key_terms.قُبِضَ: passed away; a reverential expression for death in the report

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about keeping a lamp in the house after an Imam’s death?
ai.summary: This report narrates that after the passing of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, a lamp was maintained in his residence by order of Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, and the same practice was continued by Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام in the house of Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. The narration preserves a historical detail connected to the conduct surrounding the homes of the Imams عليهم السلام after death.
